key_insight: TDAL learns how to select perturbation experiments as screening progresses, balancing immediate hits with future discoveries instead of using a fixed acquisition function.
clinical_relevance: More efficient genetic and drug perturbation screening could support cancer target discovery, but the abstract does not establish clinical benefit.
method: Learns an acquisition function online using temporal difference learning from a single screening trajectory.
Uses Hellinger distance between updated hit probabilities to weight future discovery value.
Reuses measured outcomes through leave-batch-out virtual transitions to address sparse training data.
evidence_signal: Across eight public screens covering single, double, and triple perturbations, TDAL achieved an average rank of 1.63 among 11 methods and ranked first on four tasks.
watch_item: Benchmark rankings do not establish prospective laboratory performance or quantify experimental cost savings.
paper_title: Beyond Fixed Acquisition Functions: Temporal Difference Active Learning for Perturbation Discovery
